title: Clothing Defects Kill Brand Loyalty — Survey
paragraphs: You bought a sweater a month ago and it's already got a hole in it. What do you do? Never buy from the brand again?
According to a new survey by recycling company Samsara Eco, many people walk away from the brand.
The company spoke to over 5,000 people in 120 countries about what they expect from the clothes they buy. The participants were mostly young, with 87% aged between 18 and 24.
The results found that when people have a problem with a garment, 28% would stop buying from the brand — and 16% of those people would never buy from the brand again!
Just 6% said they would return the garment, which means that companies are losing customers but not learning about quality issues.
However, the largest share — 64% — simply put up with the problem, either by repairing it themselves or continuing to wear the item.

Garment failures that frustrated people the most included material thinning or developing holes, seams splitting or unraveling, and pilling, which is when small balls of fiber form on the surface of a material.
When it comes to maintaining quality, 54% of participants said it's the responsibility of clothing brands — nearly double the amount that pointed to government regulation.
The survey also asked people about their shopping habits.

More than 88% said the cost of living was affecting how they shop for clothes, with a third saying they were buying less and expecting more from each item, and 43% saying they were buying second-hand clothes. Fourteen percent also said they were choosing cheaper items.
